column1:
The FOMC’s May 1, 2019 statement highlights a strong labor market and solid overall activity, with Q1 softness in household spending and business investment and inflation below 2%, warranting a patient hold of the federal funds rate at 2.25–2.50% and IOER at 2.35% to keep the funds rate within the range. The May 2019 Financial Stability Report adds that equity market volatility had declined from late-2018 spikes and funding risks remained low, but asset valuations were elevated and corporate leverage was high (notably in leveraged loans/CLOs), leaving vulnerabilities moderate. These FSR insights temper the otherwise positive macro tone and reinforce the Fed’s cautious, dovish-leaning posture.
